newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market operations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from open market operations on Friday, analysts said.

"We have no action," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. "They have that multi-day operation in place from yesterday and the funds rate is comfortable. We think they will be able to stay out today."
The Fed added temporary reserves to the banking system on Thursday through 14-day fixed system repurchase agreements.
Fed funds were trading at 5-3/16 percent at 0930 EST/1430 GMT, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
MMS International analysts also said the Fed could refrain from open market operations on Friday. "The desk can stay out today, but we look for repos next week," MMS said.
James Glassman, vice president and senior economist at Chase Securities Inc, said that before Thursday's 14-day operation, the Fed's "add need" stood at $9.0 billion.
"The Fed is able to (add) a lot more (reserves to the banking system) than people thought by coming in early in the morning," he said.
The Fed's typical time for open market operations is around 1130 EST/1630 GMT. But the Fed conducted its Thursday operation nearer 1030 EST/1530 GMT.
The banking system's need for reserves builds next week with the corporate tax date on Monday, analysts said.
-- Ellen Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679
